commit_message.description: Only when this job lets you write files: the commit message for what you wrote this turn, in the repository's style.

mode.description: What this issue needs: notes alone, a spec, or several issues (multi), suggested in sub_issues.

sub_issues.description: Only when the work is several changes that each merge on their own, or when Dr K asks for more: the sub-issues to suggest, in the order to do them. Dr K ticks the ones to file.

why.description: One line: what this part is, and why it is its own issue.

report.description: Only on a sub-issue, when the parent has something to act on: your homework is done, your spec is ready, or you are stuck. What you did, where your spec stands, and what you need from the parent. Posted on the parent, which it wakes. Or on a downstream issue (one adopting an upstream epic's release): posted on the epic, which it wakes; your questions about the release go here.

actions.description: On the parent of a running family: what the family does next, in order; n8n carries them out and stops at the first that fails. Empty when there is nothing to do.

kind.description: file {type, title, ask}: a new sub-issue. message {number, text, repo?}: words for one sub-issue's agent, or for the code agent of the family's open pull request to main; with repo, for a downstream issue's agent there. approve_spec {number, repo?}: a sub-issue's spec is ready; its pull request opens; with repo, a downstream issue's. approve_plan {number, repo?}: the plan on a sub-issue's pull request is ready; its code starts; with repo, the plan on a downstream issue's pull request. open_pr {}: open the family's pull request to main, ready and in review, or refresh the one open; sub-issues may still be open. ask_owner {question}: the last resort; it stops the family until Dr K answers. release_level {level}: the release this family's merge makes, set as its release label, at the latest by the first prerelease. prerelease {summary}: cut a pre-release (an rc) from the family's branch for the downstream projects to adopt; the first opens one upgrade issue in each, a later one is a message to them. One epic per upstream may have rcs out at a time.

number.description: message: the sub-issue, the family's open pull request to main, or with repo the downstream issue. approve_spec, approve_plan: the sub-issue, or with repo the downstream issue.

repo.description: message, approve_spec, approve_plan: a downstream repo, owner/name, whose issue number names; leave it out for this repo.

ask.description: file: what it is, and why it is its own issue.

question.description: ask_owner: the question for Dr K.

summary.description: prerelease: what this rc brings the downstream projects, in a few lines; it goes in their upgrade issues.

open_questions.description: On the parent, every turn: the whole running list of questions and problems for Dr K that don't block, kept current. It is posted on the family's pull request to main.

text.description: The question or problem, in one short line.

from.description: The sub-issue it came from, if any.
